line: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Nb3 e5 f3
teaches: When the centralised knight retreats, the central pawn advance it was preventing becomes available at full value — no tricks left to fall into, a full share of the centre gained. An opponent mixing two systems usually pays exactly here: each half-system allows the resource the other one was built to prevent.
explains: The pawn stands on e5 holding d4 and f4, claimed for free the moment the knight stepped back to b3, and the reply mixes systems — the modest pawn move belongs to a setup whose knight is supposed to still be in the centre. The opening argument is already won on move six.
structural: the central stake collected the move the knight retreated — mixed systems each allowing the other's antidote
